content.text:
Nature and science facts about the octopus

The octopus's eight arms are covered with countless suckers that grab objects and even taste. To blend in with its surroundings, it changes the color and pattern of its body in an instant to hide (camouflage), and when danger comes it squirts ink to cloud its enemy's eyes before slipping away. Thanks to its soft, boneless body, it can squeeze into gaps narrower than itself. This clever problem-solver is a sea friend that amazes even scientists.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How does an octopus hide itself?
A. It camouflages by instantly changing the color and pattern of its body to match its surroundings. When in danger, it also squirts ink.

Q. What do an octopus's suckers do?
A. They grab objects and even taste. There are a great many suckers along the eight arms.

Q. How can we observe it at home?
A. It's great to compare it to a chameleon's color changes and to compare the number of suckers to your fingers.
